what_its_for: Benztropine is used to treat symptoms of Parkinson's disease, such as tremors, stiffness, and slow movements. It is also used to treat movement side effects (like muscle stiffness, spasms, or restlessness) caused by certain psychiatric medications called antipsychotics.
how_to_take: Take benztropine by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it exactly as your doctor tells you — do not take more or less than prescribed. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it to find the right amount for you. The usual dose ranges from 0.5 mg to 6 mg per day, taken once a day or divided into smaller doses throughout the day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store benztropine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking benztropine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Try to stay cool and avoid getting overheated, since benztropine can reduce your ability to sweat and raise your body temperature. Avoid taking antacids within 1 to 2 hours of your dose. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially cold or allergy medicines, sleeping pills, or other medications that cause drowsiness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: fast or irregular heartbeat, trouble urinating or not being able to urinate, severe constipation or stomach pain, confusion, hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), memory problems, high fever with no sweating, eye pain or vision changes, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your symptoms within a few days of starting benztropine. However, it may take several weeks to feel the full benefit. Be patient and keep taking it as prescribed even if you do not notice immediate changes.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older) are more sensitive to the side effects of benztropine, especially confusion, memory problems, and difficulty urinating. Use with extra caution in elderly patients. This medication is generally not recommended for children under 3 years of age. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking benztropine, as its safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not well established. Use with caution if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, heart problems, or a history of bowel obstruction.
